The Ranch That Wanted to Be a Colonial

BLOG POST #1

Why This Page Exists

Every house hunt has a moment where it stops being browsing and starts being a project. Ours was a ranch on Balsam Drive in Chelmsford — a perfectly ordinary single-storey house that we immediately wanted to turn into something it wasn't. Could the town even allow a second floor on top? What would that cost? And while we were at it: new doors everywhere, a full repaint, a new kitchen countertop.

So the house got investigated properly. Zoning first. Structure second. Then the money — the renovation priced out line by line, resale comps for a ~3,000 sq ft Chelmsford home checked, and the whole thing run twice: once with the second floor, once without. With it: roughly $1.28M all-in against a value of about $1.0–1.05M. Without it: about $732k in, roughly break-even. The dream floor was the thing that sank it.

A blog, because one spreadsheet wasn't enough

That investigation was too good to leave in a chat window. Every serious house deserves the same treatment — and a public verdict. So this page exists: a cooking-blog-style journal where each house is a recipe that either works or doesn't, stamped at the end — bought, or rejected, with the reason written on the stamp.

The rules of the kitchen

Every home, buy or lease, goes through the same routine. It gets its own post, and the post's background is that home's own street view or best view — rated by Parthey before anything is published. Eight standard questions get answered for every property before a verdict (they live under The Questions in the menu). Towns get their own filters as the hunt widens. And nothing here is decoration: if a number is on a post, it came from the investigation.

House #1 is already up — the ranch that wanted to be a colonial, rejected on the value maths. The shutter is open. Send the next listing.

The Donnell Khanderia Questions

The eight answers Parthey gives in the Muse chat for every property — before any verdict. They go on the home's post, next to the investigation, and the stamp only lands once they're answered.

About Donnell Khanderia House Search

Donnell Khanderia House Search is Parthey's house-hunting journal. The home page is two photo screens side by side — Buy on one side, Lease on the other — and each home on a side gets its own framed picture, so the side with more homes takes more of the screen and the seam between them lands where the counts put it. Tap a side or any picture and its details open right there, over the split. Every home gets its own post: written up from a real investigation or a real tour, backgrounded by the home's own photo, and carrying its status — in review, or stamped with a verdict and the reason.

What's on it now

Buy — 1 home. 3 Balsam Dr, Chelmsford: the ranch that wanted a second floor. Fully investigated — zoning, structure, full costs and comps, run twice, with and without the addition — and stamped rejected on the value maths.

Lease — 2 buildings. Toured with Shannon on Saturday, Nov 7, 2026: the Towers at Longfellow in Boston — five units (4-3011, 4-1109, 1-315, 1-1020 and 3-607) listed under one picture of the building — and 315 on A, unit #1405, in Fort Point. All six units are posted In Review, tour notes and all; their final verdicts wait on Parthey's review.

How a home gets on here

1 · Send the listing. A new home is added by sending its listing in the Muse chat — that's the only way in. No forms, no uploads here.
2 · It gets investigated — or toured. Buys get the full work-up: zoning, structure, costs and sold comps. Rentals get walked and scored on a real tour. Either way it becomes a post, backgrounded by the home's own photo.
3 · Answer the eight questions. Parthey answers the eight Donnell Khanderia Questions in the chat for every property, and rates the post's background — score it too low and a better view is found first.
4 · Posted in review, then stamped. A home can go up stamped In Review while it waits; once Parthey has reviewed it, the final verdict — bought, leased, or rejected, with the reason — lands on the post and the card.

Only real homes from the hunt appear here — no examples, no placeholders. New ones join as the hunt goes on.
